p: Southampton's surroundings have a few lesser-known gems that work well with a treetop day. Netley Abbey, on the shore of Southampton Water, is a remarkably complete medieval abbey ruin and a lovely, atmospheric place for a wander. Right next door, the Royal Victoria Country Park has woodland, open lawns and views of passing ships, plus a little steam railway on some days.

Back in the city, the Bargate, the great medieval gateway in the centre, is a reminder of how old the place really is. Mayflower Park on the waterfront is named after the famous ship that set sail from here in 1620, and it's a good spot for watching cruise liners and container ships glide past.

For the Go Ape course, plan on a couple of hours including the briefing, and arrive in good time, because finding your way into a woodland site can take longer than you'd expect. If you're coming straight from a long drive or a ferry, grab a snack and stretch your legs before you start climbing.

First-timers often find the trickiest bit is the very first ladder. Once you've done that, confidence builds quickly. Pace yourself on the crossings, keep breathing and enjoy the view from each platform.
Bring water, a layer and a towel for afterwards. Hampshire summers can be warm, and you'll work up a sweat in the canopy.
